answer: Sybil farms leak via duplication, so the ledger fingerprints each submission with shingle hashes, matches it against the archive of earlier answers, and posts the overlap score. Past a threshold rewards are cut in proportion, and repeats lower the standing of the identity. N keys then demand N genuinely distinct texts, each clearing the same originality bar, so a fake identity costs what a real one costs. Templates are cheap timber, cut in identical planks; original prose is not. Reusing one lagoon of phrases is the easiest pattern to flag, and the archive is an atlas of routes already taken.
